In Willow Creek, green and deep,
Where secrets old, the forest keep,
Lived Lumi, a firefly so small,
Afraid to shine, afraid to fall.

Her light was dim, a tiny spark,
Compared to others, in the dark.
"I'm not enough," she'd often sigh,
And watch the brighter fireflies fly.

One night, the Elder, wise and old,
A story to the fireflies told.
Of Whisperwind, a magical tree,
Whose light was fading, tragically.

"Its leaves are dull, its branches weak,
Unless a firefly, brave and meek,
Can bring a spark, of purest light,
To heal the tree, and make it bright."

The other fireflies, they buzzed and gleamed,
Eager to help, so it seemed.
But when they flew towards the wood,
A fearsome shadow understood.

A grumpy Grumblebug, so big and mean,
Guarded the tree, a sight unseen.
He hated light, he hated glee,
And chased the fireflies angrily.

They scattered fast, they flew away,
Determined not to fight this day.
Lumi watched them, filled with fear,
But something whispered in her ear.

"You are the one," a voice so clear,
Dispelling all her doubt and fear.
She thought about the wilting tree.
"I must be brave, this I can see."

Lumi flew on, against the breeze,
Past rustling leaves, and whispering trees.
She reached the Grumblebug, so vast,
And knew this moment had arrived at last.

He roared a challenge, loud and strong,
"Get out of here! You don't belong!"
Lumi felt her wings begin to shake,
A coping moment, for goodness sake.

She took a breath, "I will not flee!
I'm here to help the Whisperwind Tree!"
The Grumblebug just laughed with scorn,
"Your tiny light is barely born!"

But Lumi, with determination true,
Flew closer, knowing what to do.
She concentrated, closed her eyes,
And focused on the starlit skies.

Suddenly, her light grew strong and bright,
A magical surprise, filling the night.
Not just a flicker, but a beam,
The purest light, a vibrant dream.

The Grumblebug, he gasped in shock,
He stumbled back, around the rock.
Lumi flew towards the fading tree,
And touched a branch, so tenderly.

The Whisperwind began to glow,
Its leaves turned green, in vibrant flow.
The tree was healed, its magic free,
Thanks to Lumi, brave as can be.

The other fireflies returned with cheer,
Their doubts replaced by joy so clear.
And Lumi, once afraid to shine,
Now knew her light, was truly divine. "I must be brave, this I can see."
